text:
mika: FYI seeing a weird init-frame pause when opening the dashboard time selector. charts request completes but there's a 250-700ms hang before first paint. happens more with heatmap + sparklines together. any ideas?

samir: curious — did you repro on canary or prod? we've got the telemetry client rolled to canary yesterday (v1.14.0) which changed the metric batcher. could be backpressure in the render pipeline.

mika: hit it on prod and locally on prod build+canary config. reproduces intermittently when switching 1h -> 24h ranges. not all users.

jodie: I saw a bundle bump in the telemetry chunk around the same time. surface-level diff shows a new dependency that touched the hot-path. diff: `+ node_modules/telemetry-client/dist/metrics.js (+12KB)`

samir: hmmm. two things to check: (1) KV prewarm/prefetch misses — we recently changed prefetch windowing to 300ms debounce, might be dropping some early requests; (2) module-splitting: the telemetry chunk may be delaying main thread while it evals.

mika: sample logs from the client when it stalls: 
```
[metrics] batch_send_start t=0
[network] fetch heatmap 200 t=120
[render] waitForPaint t=520 (blocked)
[metrics] batch_send_done t=560
```

ana: @samir can the prefetch debounce be tuned? if prefetch kicks in too late the KV cache miss causes a synchronous fallback path that hits the main thread.

samir: yep we can tune, but curious if it's the right fix. alternatives: (A) shift the KV prewarm earlier during route transition, (B) make telemetry send non-blocking (fire-and-forget) or offload to a microtask, (C) revert the telemetry client change.

jodie: option B seems safest short-term. the telemetry client now awaits a batch ack before resolving which can block some UI promises. patch idea:
```js
// telemetry client
sendBatch(batch) {
  navigator.sendBeacon?.(url, batch) || fetch(url, { body: batch, keepalive: true });
  // do not await response in hot-path
}
```

mika: +1 for fire-and-forget. but if we do that we lose immediate error telemetry for rollouts. tradeoff ok for canary though.

ana: also check routing: console's API proxy will route heavy chart queries to the low-priority pool if caller is over quota. if a bunch of those fall back to compact endpoints, we could be seeing serialization differences that block the renderer.

samir: good catch. I pulled routing logs and saw ~12% of these user requests in the window were re-routed to the quota-fallback path at 11:32 PST. fallback path adds a JSON post-processing step sync on main thread in current client. that's probably it.

mika: oh nice find. so we have three interacting factors: telemetry client awaiting, prefetch debounce too aggressive, and routing fallback hitting a slow client-side post-process.

jodie: propose prioritized plan: 1) hotfix telemetry client to not block (canary rollout within 2 hrs), 2) lower prefetch debounce to 100ms and add a KV prewarm on route-start, 3) remove main-thread postprocess from fallback path or move it to worker.

samir: agree. I'll open a PR for (1) and (2). tagging @deploy-bot to kick a canary after merge.

deploy-bot: canary pipeline triggered for frontend-canary at sha=ab12c9. started at 2217654550. notify: #deploys

mika: thanks. I'll keep an eye on SLOs and telemetry. if the canary looks good we'll roll to prod tonight. :thumbsup:

jodie: also logging note — add an explicit metric for "render-handoff-block-ms" so we can alert when >200ms p95. saves chasing these multi-factor regressions later.

samir: will add the metric and a short dashboard panel. once canary stabilizes we'll check correlation between routing-fallback rate and render-handoff metric.

mika: sounds like a plan. I'll update the incident doc with steps and link once PRs land.

ana: great work team.
